subject: TYPE clause
notes: kb/Work PB1300. Rule (cite.py --check 13.18.57.4 'excluding the level-number, name, alignment, and the GLOBAL, SELECT WHEN, and TYPEDEF clauses specified for type-name-1' -> OK §13.18.57.4 1); 13.18.58.4 'All other data description clauses and subordinate data descriptions are assumed by data defined using the type-name' -> OK 3)). The one description copy (CopyEntryDescription) carries every clause but the exclusions; BASED is now DescriptionCopyKind.EntryOnly (carried by TYPE / SAME AS / subordinate copies, not onto a compiler temporary), so `01 T TYPEDEF BASED PIC X(5). 01 X TYPE T.` makes X a based item: SET ADDRESS OF X TO ADDRESS OF Y then X=[HELLO], MOVE to X writes Y (positive golden). A composed BASED is placement-screened as a written one (ScreenComposedBased, COBOL2510: §13.16.3 SR16 level 1/77, SR5 not with EXTERNAL, SR13 not with CONSTANT RECORD) - `05 X TYPE T` is refused (negative golden). SR16's SECTION sentence is owned by kb/Work PB516 for both arms (BasedLevelAdmitted is the shared predicate). The alignment exclusion (scope TypeSubject), level-number/name and TYPEDEF behave as before (probe t1 of the adjudication).
